challenge.reason: The supersession argument is unsound. The old decision is a security invariant: secrets come from environment variables only and are never written to the repo or to .faff/. The new decision writes resolved API keys in plaintext to .faff/cache/credentials.json, which breaks the 'never written to .faff/' clause directly; the why only addresses the repo-commit half. Being gitignored does not stop the file being read by other local processes, copied by backups, swept into run-directory archives or bug-report bundles, or left behind after a key is rotated or revoked, so a stale key keeps being used. The claim of 'no behaviour change a user would notice' is false for exactly those cases. The benefit is not established: process.env is an in-memory lookup in Node, so per-call cost is negligible next to an LLM network round trip, and if it mattered, caching the value in process memory for the session gives the same saving without persisting a secret to disk. The why does not show that the old decision's premise has stopped holding; it trades a standing security guarantee for an unmeasured micro-optimisation.
